summary: The proof is sequentially valid. The normalization and no-half condition force k/M to 1, the crossing and tail identities force p_empty/M and the three middle-cap fractions to their claimed limits, and John normalization yields a nondegenerate Hausdorff limit. The planar Grunbaum equality characterization applies exactly and forces the limiting body and cuts to be the three distinct centroidal vertex caps of a triangle. The common lower-offset triangles then converge back to that limit. Finite-stage positivity of each all-double Q-cell supplies the three midpoint inequalities needed to confine P_empty to the truncated barycentric simplex, whose stated area formula and uniform bound give liminf k/p_empty at least 3/2, contradicting k/p_empty tending to 1. Boundary conventions, vanishing cap-ratio limits, and the eventual positivity needed for the ambient-triangle predecessor fact are all covered.
